title.zh: 卷一百四十二 列傳第九十二: 李寶臣 王武俊 王廷湊
title.en: Volume 142 Biographies 92: Li Baochen, Wang Wujun, Wang Tingcou
title.raw: 卷一百四十二 列傳第九十二: 李寶臣 王武俊 王廷湊 Volume 142 Biographies 92: Li Baochen, Wang Wujun, Wang Tingcou

sentences.zh: 李寶臣，范陽城旁奚族也。

translations.literal: Li Baochen was of the Xi tribe beside Fanyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baochen belonged to the Xi people who lived near Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 故范陽將張鎖高之假子，故姓張，名忠誌。

translations.literal: He was the adopted son of the former Fanyang general Zhang Suogao; he therefore bore the surname Zhang and was named Zhongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was the adopted son of the former Fanyang general Zhang Suogao and originally bore the surname Zhang, with the personal name Zhongzhi.

sentences.zh: 幼善騎射，節度使安祿山選為射生官。

translations.literal: From youth he excelled at riding and archery; Military Commissioner An Lushan selected him as a shooting-life officer.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he excelled at riding and archery, and Military Commissioner An Lushan selected him as a shooting-life officer.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，隨祿山入朝，玄宗留為射生子弟，出入禁中。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he followed Lushan to court; Emperor Xuanzong retained him among the shooting-life youths, and he came and went within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he accompanied Lushan to court. Emperor Xuanzong kept him among the shooting-life youths, and he moved freely within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 及祿山叛，忠誌遁歸范陽；

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Zhongzhi fled back to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, Zhongzhi fled back to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祿山喜，錄為假子，姓安，常給事帳中。

translations.literal: Lushan was pleased, enrolled him as an adopted son, gave him the surname An, and regularly had him serve in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was pleased, took him as an adopted son, gave him the surname An, and regularly kept him at work in headquarters.

sentences.zh: 祿山兵將指闕，使忠誌領驍騎八千人入太原，劫太原尹楊光翙。

translations.literal: When Lushan's army was about to march on the capital, he sent Zhongzhi to lead eight thousand crack cavalry into Taiyuan and seize Taiyuan prefect Yang Guanghui.
translations.idiomatic: As Lushan's army was about to march on the capital, he sent Zhongzhi at the head of eight thousand crack horsemen into Taiyuan to seize Prefect Yang Guanghui.

sentences.zh: 忠誌挾光翙出太原，萬兵追之不敢近。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi took Guanghui out of Taiyuan; ten thousand troops pursued but dared not come near.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi marched Guanghui out of Taiyuan. Ten thousand pursuers followed but dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 祿山使董精甲，扼井陘路，軍於土門。

translations.literal: Lushan sent Dong Jingjia with picked armor to hold the Jingxing road and encamp at Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent Dong Jingjia with elite troops to hold the Jingxing road and encamp at Tumen.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒偽署為恆州刺史。

translations.literal: An Qingxu falsely appointed him prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu falsely appointed him prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 九節度之師圍慶緒於相州，忠誌懼，獻章歸國，肅宗因授恆州刺史。

translations.literal: When the armies of the nine commissioners besieged Qingxu at Xiangzhou, Zhongzhi grew afraid, submitted a memorial returning to the state, and Emperor Suzong thereupon appointed him prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of nine commissioners besieged Qingxu at Xiangzhou, Zhongzhi grew afraid, submitted a memorial pledging allegiance to the dynasty, and Emperor Suzong appointed him prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 及史思明復渡河，偽授忠誌工部尚書、恆州刺史、恆趙節度使，統眾三萬守常山。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming again crossed the Yellow River, he falsely appointed Zhongzhi Minister of Works, prefect of Hengzhou, and military commissioner of Heng and Zhao, commanding thirty thousand men to hold Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming again crossed the Yellow River, he falsely appointed Zhongzhi Minister of Works, prefect of Hengzhou, and commissioner of Heng and Zhao, with thirty thousand men to hold Changshan.

sentences.zh: 及思明敗，不受朝義之命，乃開土門路以內王師。

translations.literal: When Siming was defeated, he would not accept Chaoyi's orders and opened the Tumen road to admit the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: After Siming's defeat he refused Chaoyi's orders and opened the Tumen road to admit the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 河朔平定，忠誌與李懷仙、薛嵩、田承嗣各舉其地歸國，皆賜鐵券，誓以不死。

translations.literal: When the Hebei region was pacified, Zhongzhi together with Li Huaixian, Xue Song, and Tian Chengsi each offered their territories in submission to the state; all were granted iron tallies pledging they would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hebei region was pacified, Zhongzhi together with Li Huaixian, Xue Song, and Tian Chengsi each submitted their territories to the dynasty. All were granted iron tallies pledging immunity from execution.

sentences.zh: 因授忠誌開府儀同三司、檢校禮部尚書、恆州刺史，實封二百戶，仍舊為節度使。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi was then appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of opening an office, Acting Minister of Rites, and prefect of Hengzhou, with a substantive fief of two hundred households, and he continued as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi was then appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with privilege to open an office, Acting Minister of Rites, and prefect of Hengzhou, with a substantive fief of two hundred households, while continuing as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乃以恆州為成德軍，賜姓名曰李寶臣。

translations.literal: Hengzhou was made the Chengde Army, and the surname and name Li Baochen were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhou was made the seat of the Chengde Army, and he received the surname and name Li Baochen.

sentences.zh: 時寶臣有恆、定、易、趙、深、冀六州之地，後又得滄州，步卒五萬、馬五千匹，當時勇冠河朔諸帥。

translations.literal: At that time Baochen held the six prefectures of Heng, Ding, Yi, Zhao, Shen, and Ji, and later gained Cangzhou as well: fifty thousand infantry and five thousand horses, the boldest of all the Hebei commanders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Baochen held Heng, Ding, Yi, Zhao, Shen, and Ji, and later gained Cangzhou as well—fifty thousand foot soldiers and five thousand horses, the boldest commander in all Hebei.

sentences.zh: 寶臣以七州自給，軍用殷積，招集亡命之徒，繕閱兵仗，與薛嵩、田承嗣、李正己、梁崇義等連結姻婭，互為表裏，意在以土地傳付子孫，不稟朝旨，自補官吏，不輸王賦。

translations.literal: Baochen supplied himself from seven prefectures; his military stores were abundant. He gathered fugitives, reviewed arms, and with Xue Song, Tian Chengsi, Li Zhengji, and Liang Chongyi formed marriage alliances and mutual support, intending to pass the land to his descendants. He did not follow court orders, appointed officials himself, and did not remit imperial taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen supplied his army from seven prefectures and amassed abundant stores. He gathered fugitives, drilled his arms, and with Xue Song, Tian Chengsi, Li Zhengji, and Liang Chongyi formed marriage ties and mutual backing, intending to pass his lands to his descendants. He ignored court orders, appointed his own officials, and withheld imperial taxes.

sentences.zh: 初，天寶中，天下州郡皆鑄銅為玄宗真容，擬佛之制。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Tianbao era, every commandery and prefecture in the realm cast bronze images of Emperor Xuanzong's true likeness, following the Buddhist model.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Tianbao era, every commandery and prefecture in the realm cast bronze images of Emperor Xuanzong's true likeness, following the Buddhist model.

sentences.zh: 及安、史之亂，賊之所部，悉熔毀之，而恆州獨存，由是實封百戶。

translations.literal: In the disorders of An and Shi, wherever the rebels passed, the images were melted and destroyed; only Hengzhou's survived, and for this he received an added fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the disorders of An and Shi, the rebels melted and destroyed the images wherever they passed; only Hengzhou's survived, and for this he received an added fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 初，寶臣、正己皆為承嗣所易。

translations.literal: Earlier, both Baochen and Zhengji had been outmaneuvered by Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, both Baochen and Zhengji had been outmaneuvered by Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 寶臣弟寶正娶承嗣女，在魏州與承嗣子維擊鞠，寶正馬馳駭，觸殺維。

translations.literal: Baochen's younger brother Baozheng married Chengsi's daughter; at Weizhou he played cuju with Chengsi's son Wei, and Baozheng's horse bolted in fright and struck Wei dead.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen's younger brother Baozheng married Chengsi's daughter. At Weizhou he played cuju with Chengsi's son Wei; Baozheng's horse bolted in fright and struck Wei dead.

sentences.zh: 承嗣怒，縶寶正以告。

translations.literal: Chengsi was enraged, seized Baozheng, and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was enraged, seized Baozheng, and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 寶臣謝為教不謹，緘杖令承嗣以示責，承嗣遂鞭殺之，由是交惡。

translations.literal: Baochen apologized for lax discipline, bound the cane and sent it to Chengsi to show his reproof; Chengsi then flogged Baozheng to death, and from this their relations turned hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen apologized for lax discipline, sent a bound cane to Chengsi as a token of reproof, and Chengsi then flogged Baozheng to death. From this their relations turned hostile.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年，寶臣、正己更言承嗣之罪，請討之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of the Dali era, Baochen and Zhengji again denounced Chengsi's crimes and asked to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Dali, Baochen and Zhengji again denounced Chengsi's crimes and asked permission to attack him.

sentences.zh: 代宗欲因其相圖，乃從其請。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong wished to profit from their mutual strife and granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong wished to profit from their mutual strife and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 時幽州節度留後硃滔方恭順朝廷，詔滔與寶臣及太原之師攻其北，正己與滑亳、河陽、江淮之師攻其南。

translations.literal: At that time Youzhou acting military commissioner Zhu Tao was still deferential to the court; an edict ordered Tao together with Baochen and the Taiyuan forces to attack from the north, and Zhengji with the Hua-Bo, Heyang, and Jiang-Huai forces to attack from the south.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Youzhou acting commissioner Zhu Tao was still deferential to the court. An edict ordered Tao and Baochen, together with the Taiyuan army, to attack from the north, and Zhengji with the Hua-Bo, Heyang, and Jiang-Huai armies to attack from the south.

sentences.zh: 寶臣、正己會軍於棗強，椎牛釃酒，犒勞將士，仍頒優賞。

translations.literal: Baochen and Zhengji joined forces at Zaoqiang, slaughtered oxen and poured wine, rewarded the officers and men, and also issued special bonuses.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen and Zhengji joined forces at Zaoqiang, slaughtered oxen and poured wine to reward the troops, and also issued special bonuses.

sentences.zh: 寶臣軍賞厚，正己軍賞薄。

translations.literal: Baochen's army received generous rewards; Zhengji's received meager ones.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen's army received generous rewards; Zhengji's received meager ones.

sentences.zh: 既罷會，正己軍中咄咄有辭，正己聞，懼有變，即時引退。

translations.literal: When the meeting ended, Zhengji's troops murmured complaints; Zhengji heard and, fearing mutiny, withdrew at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the meeting ended, Zhengji's troops murmured complaints. Zhengji heard them, feared mutiny, and withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 由是寶臣、硃滔共攻承嗣之滄州，連年未下。

translations.literal: Thereafter Baochen and Zhu Tao jointly attacked Chengsi's Cangzhou, but for years could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Baochen and Zhu Tao jointly attacked Chengsi's Cangzhou, but for years could not take it.

sentences.zh: 時承嗣使腹心將盧子期攻邢州，城將陷，寶臣發精卒赴救，擊敗之，擒子期來獻。

translations.literal: At that time Chengsi sent his trusted general Lu Ziqi to attack Xingzhou; as the city was about to fall, Baochen sent elite troops to the rescue, defeated him, captured Ziqi, and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chengsi sent his trusted general Lu Ziqi to attack Xingzhou. As the city was about to fall, Baochen sent elite troops to the rescue, defeated him, captured Ziqi, and presented him as a prize.

sentences.zh: 河南諸將又大破田悅於陳留，正己收承嗣之德州，以重兵臨其境，指期進討。

translations.literal: The Henan commanders again heavily defeated Tian Yue at Chenliu; Zhengji recovered Chengsi's Dezhou and with a strong force pressed the border, set on advancing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan commanders again heavily defeated Tian Yue at Chenliu. Zhengji recovered Chengsi's Dezhou and with a strong force pressed the border, set on advancing to attack.

sentences.zh: 承嗣大懾，遂求解於寶臣，寶臣不許。

translations.literal: Chengsi was greatly terrified and sought terms from Baochen; Baochen would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was greatly terrified and sought terms from Baochen, but Baochen would not agree.

sentences.zh: 初，正己將發兵，使人至魏，承嗣囚之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhengji was about to send troops, he sent a man to Wei; Chengsi imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhengji was about to send troops, he sent a man to Wei; Chengsi imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 及是，乃厚禮遣歸，發使與俱，具列境內戶口兵糧之數，悉以奉正己。

translations.literal: Now he treated him with great courtesy and sent him back, dispatching an envoy with him and listing in full the households, troops, and grain within his borders, offering all to Zhengji.
translations.idiomatic: Now he treated the man with great courtesy and sent him back, dispatching an envoy with him and listing in full the households, troops, and grain within his borders, offering all to Zhengji.

sentences.zh: 且告曰：「承嗣老矣，今年八十有六，形體支離，無日月焉。

translations.literal: He also said: "Chengsi is old; this year he is eighty-six, his body broken and disjointed, with no days left.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Chengsi is old. This year he is eighty-six; his body is broken and disjointed, and he has no days left.

sentences.zh: 己子不令，悅亦孱弱，不足保其後業。

translations.literal: My son is unworthy, and Yue is also feeble; they cannot preserve the inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: My son is unworthy, and Yue is also feeble—they cannot preserve what I leave behind.

sentences.zh: 今之所有，為公守耳，曷足辱公師旅焉！」

translations.literal: What I now possess I hold for you—how could it be worth troubling your armies!"
translations.idiomatic: What I now possess I hold for you—how could it be worth troubling your armies!"

sentences.zh: 立使者於廷，南向，拜而授書。

translations.literal: He stood the envoy in the hall, faced south, bowed, and handed over the letter.
translations.idiomatic: He stood the envoy in the hall, faced south, bowed, and handed over the letter.

sentences.zh: 又圖正己形，焚香事之如神，謂人曰：「真聖人也！」

translations.literal: He also had Zhengji's likeness painted, burned incense and served it like a god, and said to people: "A true sage!"
translations.idiomatic: He also had Zhengji's likeness painted, burned incense and served it like a god, and said to people, "A true sage!"

sentences.zh: 正己聞之，且得其歡，乃止諸軍，莫敢進者。

translations.literal: Zhengji heard this and, having won his favor, then halted the armies; none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji heard this and, having won his favor, halted the armies; none dared advance.

sentences.zh: 承嗣止正己，無南軍之虞。

translations.literal: Chengsi halted Zhengji and had no worry from the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi halted Zhengji and had no worry from the southern army.

sentences.zh: 又知范陽寶臣故裏，生長其間，心常欲得之；

translations.literal: He also knew that Fanyang was Baochen's native place and that he had grown up there; Baochen's heart had long desired to possess it.
translations.idiomatic: He also knew that Fanyang was Baochen's native place and that he had grown up there; Baochen had long desired to possess it.

sentences.zh: 乃勒石為讖，密瘞寶臣境內，使望氣者云：「此中有玉氣。」

translations.literal: He then carved a stone prophecy and secretly buried it within Baochen's territory, and had a geomancer say: "There is jade vapor within this place."
translations.idiomatic: He then carved a stone prophecy and secretly buried it within Baochen's territory, and had a geomancer say, "There is jade vapor within this place."

sentences.zh: 寶臣掘地得之，有文曰：「二帝同功勢萬全，將田作伴入幽、燕。」

translations.literal: Baochen dug and found it; the inscription read: "Two emperors share merit and power is wholly secure; take Tian as companion and enter You and Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Baochen dug and found it. The inscription read, "Two emperors share merit and power is wholly secure; take Tian as companion and enter You and Yan."

sentences.zh: 二帝，指寶臣、正己也。

translations.literal: The two emperors referred to Baochen and Zhengji.
translations.idiomatic: The two emperors referred to Baochen and Zhengji.

sentences.zh: 承嗣又使客諷之曰：「公與硃滔共舉，取吾滄州，設得之，當歸國，非公所有。

translations.literal: Chengsi also sent a guest to hint to him: "You and Zhu Tao are jointly raising troops to take my Cangzhou; if you get it, it will return to the state and will not be yours.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi also sent a guest to hint to him, "You and Zhu Tao are jointly raising troops to take my Cangzhou. If you get it, it will return to the state and will not be yours.

sentences.zh: 誠能舍承嗣之罪，請以滄州奉獻，可不勞師而致，願取范陽以自效。

translations.literal: If you can pardon Chengsi's crime, I ask to offer Cangzhou in submission; you can gain it without troubling your armies. I wish to take Fanyang to prove my loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: If you can pardon Chengsi's crime, I ask to offer Cangzhou in submission—you can gain it without troubling your armies. I wish to take Fanyang to prove my loyalty.

sentences.zh: 公將騎為前驅，承嗣率步卒從，此萬全之勢。」

translations.literal: You will ride as vanguard; Chengsi will follow with infantry—this is a wholly secure position."
translations.idiomatic: You will ride as vanguard; Chengsi will follow with infantry—this is a wholly secure position."

sentences.zh: 寶臣喜，以為事合符命，遂與承嗣通謀，割州與之。

translations.literal: Baochen was pleased, thinking the matter matched the prophecy, and then conspired with Chengsi and ceded a prefecture to him.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen was pleased, thinking the matter matched the prophecy, and then conspired with Chengsi and ceded a prefecture to him.

sentences.zh: 寶臣乃密圖范陽，承嗣亦陳兵境上。

translations.literal: Baochen then secretly plotted against Fanyang, and Chengsi also arrayed troops on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen then secretly plotted against Fanyang, and Chengsi also arrayed troops on the border.

sentences.zh: 寶臣謂硃滔使曰：「吾聞硃公貌如神，安得而識之？

translations.literal: Baochen said to Zhu Tao's envoy: "I have heard that Lord Zhu's appearance is like a god's—how could I come to know him?
translations.idiomatic: Baochen said to Zhu Tao's envoy, "I have heard that Lord Zhu's appearance is like a god's—how could I come to know him?

sentences.zh: 願因繪事而觀，可乎？」

translations.literal: Might I view him through a painted likeness—would that be possible?"
translations.idiomatic: Might I view him through a painted likeness—would that be possible?"

sentences.zh: 滔乃圖其形以示之。

translations.literal: Tao then had his likeness painted and showed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao then had his likeness painted and showed it to him.

sentences.zh: 寶臣懸於射堂，命諸將熟視之，曰：「硃公信神人也！」

translations.literal: Baochen hung it in the archery hall, ordered the generals to study it closely, and said: "Lord Zhu is truly a divine man!"
translations.idiomatic: Baochen hung it in the archery hall, ordered the generals to study it closely, and said, "Lord Zhu is truly a divine man!"

sentences.zh: 他日，滔出軍，寶臣密選精卒劫之，戒其將曰：「取彼貌如射堂所懸者。」

translations.literal: Another day, when Tao marched out, Baochen secretly selected elite troops to seize him and warned his generals: "Take the one whose face matches what hangs in the archery hall."
translations.idiomatic: Another day, when Tao marched out, Baochen secretly selected elite troops to seize him and warned his generals, "Take the one whose face matches what hangs in the archery hall."

sentences.zh: 是時，二軍不相虞有變，滔與戰於瓦橋。

translations.literal: At that time the two armies did not expect treachery; Tao fought with him at Waqiao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the two armies did not expect treachery; Tao fought with him at Waqiao.

sentences.zh: 滔適衣他服，以不識免。

translations.literal: Tao happened to be wearing other clothes and escaped because he was not recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Tao happened to be wearing other clothes and escaped because he was not recognized.

sentences.zh: 承嗣聞與滔交鋒，其釁已成，乃旋軍，使告寶臣曰：「河內有警急，不暇從公。

translations.literal: Chengsi heard that he had clashed with Tao and that the breach was complete; he then turned his army and sent word to Baochen: "There is urgent alarm within the passes; I have no leisure to follow you.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi heard that he had clashed with Tao and that the breach was complete; he then turned his army and sent word to Baochen, "There is urgent alarm within the passes; I have no leisure to follow you.

sentences.zh: 石上讖文，吾戲為之耳！」

translations.literal: The prophecy on the stone—I made it in jest!"
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy on the stone—I made it in jest!"

sentences.zh: 寶臣慚怒而退。

translations.literal: Baochen withdrew in shame and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen withdrew in shame and anger.

sentences.zh: 遷左僕射，封隴西郡王、檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi, Acting Minister of Works, and Co-commissioner of the Department of State Affairs and the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi, Acting Minister of Works, and Co-commissioner of the Department of State Affairs and the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，拜司空，兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Baochen was appointed Minister of Works and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Baochen was appointed Minister of Works and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 寶臣名位既高，自擅一方，專貯異志。

translations.literal: Baochen's name and rank were already high; he controlled a region on his own and secretly harbored disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen's name and rank were already high; he controlled a region on his own and secretly harbored disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 妖人偽為讖語，言寶臣終有天位。

translations.literal: Sorcerers forged prophecies saying Baochen would ultimately attain the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Sorcerers forged prophecies saying Baochen would ultimately attain the throne.

sentences.zh: 寶臣乃為符瑞及靈芝硃草，作硃書符。

translations.literal: Baochen then made talismans and auspicious signs, lingzhi and vermilion grass, and vermilion talisman scripts.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen then made talismans and auspicious signs, lingzhi and vermilion grass, and vermilion talisman scripts.

sentences.zh: 又於深室齋戒築壇，上置金匜、玉斝，雲「甘露神酒自出」。

translations.literal: He also purified himself in a deep chamber, built an altar, placed a golden bowl and jade cup upon it, and declared that "divine wine of sweet dew would issue of itself."
translations.idiomatic: He also purified himself in a deep chamber, built an altar, placed a golden bowl and jade cup upon it, and declared that "divine wine of sweet dew would issue of itself."

sentences.zh: 又偽刻玉為印，金填文字，告境內云：「天降靈瑞，非予所求，不祈而至。」

translations.literal: He also falsely carved jade into a seal, filled the characters with gold, and announced within his territory: "Heaven has sent auspicious omens—not what I sought; they come unbidden."
translations.idiomatic: He also falsely carved jade into a seal, filled the characters with gold, and announced within his territory, "Heaven has sent auspicious omens—not what I sought; they come unbidden."

sentences.zh: 將吏無敢言者。

translations.literal: None of the officers and clerks dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: None of the officers and clerks dared speak.

sentences.zh: 妖輩慮其詐發，乃曰：「相公須飲甘露湯，即天神降。」

translations.literal: The sorcerers, fearing exposure of the fraud, then said: "The lord must drink sweet-dew broth, and then the heavenly spirit will descend."
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerers, fearing exposure of the fraud, then said, "The lord must drink sweet-dew broth, and then the heavenly spirit will descend."

sentences.zh: 寶臣然之。

translations.literal: Baochen agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen agreed.

sentences.zh: 妖人置堇湯中，飲之，三日而卒。

translations.literal: The sorcerers placed aconite in the broth; he drank it and died in three days.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerers placed aconite in the broth; he drank it and died in three days.

sentences.zh: 寶臣暮年，益多猜忌，以惟嶽暗懦，諸將不服，即殺大將辛忠義、盧俶、定州刺史張南容、趙州刺史張彭老、許崇俊等二十余人，家口沒入，自是諸將離心。

translations.literal: In his later years Baochen grew ever more suspicious. Thinking Weiyue timid and weak and that the generals would not obey him, he killed the great generals Xin Zhongyi, Lu Xu, Dingzhou prefect Zhang Nanrong, Zhao prefect Zhang Penglao, Xu Chongjun, and more than twenty others; their households were confiscated, and from this the generals turned away in heart.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Baochen grew ever more suspicious. Thinking Weiyue timid and weak and that the generals would not obey him, he killed the great generals Xin Zhongyi, Lu Xu, Dingzhou prefect Zhang Nanrong, Zhao prefect Zhang Penglao, Xu Chongjun, and more than twenty others. Their households were confiscated, and from this the generals turned away in heart.

sentences.zh: 建中二年春卒，時年六十四，廢朝三日，冊贈太保。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jianzhong he died at sixty-four; court mourning was suspended for three days, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Jianzhong he died at sixty-four. Court mourning was suspended for three days, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 子惟嶽、惟誠、惟簡。

translations.literal: His sons were Weiyue, Weicheng, and Weijian.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Weiyue, Weicheng, and Weijian.

sentences.zh: 寶臣卒時，惟嶽為行軍司馬，三軍推為留後，仍遣使上表求襲父任，朝旨不允。

translations.literal: When Baochen died, Weiyue was acting army marshal; the three armies pushed him as acting commissioner and also sent an envoy with a memorial asking to inherit his father's post; the court would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Baochen died, Weiyue was acting army marshal. The three armies pushed him as acting commissioner and sent an envoy with a memorial asking to inherit his father's post; the court would not grant it.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使田悅上章保薦，請賜旄節，不許。

translations.literal: Weibo military commissioner Tian Yue submitted a memorial recommending him and asked that the banner and baton be granted; this too was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo military commissioner Tian Yue submitted a memorial recommending him and asked that the banner and baton be granted; this too was refused.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽乃與田悅、李正己同謀拒命，判官邵真泣諫，以為不可。

translations.literal: Weiyue then conspired with Tian Yue and Li Zhengji to defy orders; judge Shao Zhen wept and remonstrated, saying it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue then conspired with Tian Yue and Li Zhengji to defy orders. Judge Shao Zhen wept and remonstrated, saying it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽暗懦，初雖聽從，終為左右所惑而止。

translations.literal: Weiyue was timid and weak; though at first he listened, in the end he was swayed by those around him and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue was timid and weak. Though at first he listened, in the end he was swayed by those around him and stopped.

sentences.zh: 而所與圖議，皆奸吏胡震、家人王他奴等，唯勸拒逆為事。

translations.literal: Those with whom he plotted were all corrupt clerks Hu Zhen and household retainer Wang Tanu and the like, who only urged resistance and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Those with whom he plotted were all corrupt clerks such as Hu Zhen and household retainer Wang Tanu, who only urged resistance and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽舅谷從政者，有智略。

translations.literal: Weiyue's maternal uncle Gu Congzheng had wisdom and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue's maternal uncle Gu Congzheng had wisdom and strategy.

sentences.zh: 為寶臣所忌，稱病不出，至是知惟嶽之謀，慮其覆宗，乃出諫惟嶽曰：「今天下無事，遠方朝貢，主上神武，必致太平。

translations.literal: Baochen had been jealous of him; he claimed illness and did not go out. Now, knowing Weiyue's plan and fearing the destruction of the clan, he came out and remonstrated with Weiyue: "Today the realm is at peace; distant regions send tribute; the sovereign is martial and divine—he is sure to bring great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen had been jealous of him; he claimed illness and did not go out. Now, knowing Weiyue's plan and fearing the destruction of the clan, he came out and remonstrated with Weiyue, "Today the realm is at peace; distant regions send tribute; the sovereign is martial and divine—he is sure to bring great peace.

sentences.zh: 如至不允，必至加兵。

translations.literal: If the request is not granted, troops are sure to be sent.
translations.idiomatic: If the request is not granted, troops are sure to be sent.

sentences.zh: 雖大夫恩及三軍，萬一不捷，孰為大夫用命者？

translations.literal: Though the lord's grace reaches the three armies, if in the end you do not prevail, who will risk his life for you?
translations.idiomatic: Though the lord's grace reaches the three armies, if in the end you do not prevail, who will risk his life for you?

sentences.zh: 又先朝相公與幽帥不協，今國家致討，必命硃滔為帥。

translations.literal: Moreover, the former lord and the Youzhou commander were not on good terms; now if the state sends punishment, Zhu Tao is sure to be made commander.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the former lord and the Youzhou commander were not on good terms. Now if the state sends punishment, Zhu Tao is sure to be made commander.

sentences.zh: 彼嘗切齒，今遂復讎，可不懼乎！

translations.literal: He once gnashed his teeth at this—now he can take revenge; should you not fear it!
translations.idiomatic: He once gnashed his teeth at this—now he can take revenge. Should you not fear it!

sentences.zh: 又頃者相公誅滅軍中將校，其子弟存者，口雖不言，心寧無憤？

translations.literal: Moreover, in recent years the lord executed commanders in the army; though their sons who remain say nothing, can their hearts be without rage?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in recent years the lord executed commanders in the army. Though their surviving sons say nothing, can their hearts be without rage?

sentences.zh: 兵猶火也，不戢自焚。

translations.literal: Soldiers are like fire; if not checked they burn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers are like fire; if not checked they burn themselves.

sentences.zh: 往者田承嗣佐安祿山、史思明謀亂天下，千征百戰。

translations.literal: In the past Tian Chengsi aided An Lushan and Shi Siming in plotting disorder throughout the realm and fought through a thousand campaigns and a hundred battles.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Tian Chengsi aided An Lushan and Shi Siming in plotting disorder throughout the realm and fought through a thousand campaigns and a hundred battles.

sentences.zh: 及頃年侵擾

translations.literal: And in recent years when he harassed
translations.idiomatic: And in recent years when he harassed

sentences.zh: 洺、相等州，為官軍所敗，及貶永州，仰天垂泣。

translations.literal: Luozhou and Xiangzhou and the like, he was defeated by the imperial army and demoted to Yongzhou, where he looked up to heaven and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou, Xiangzhou, and the like, he was defeated by the imperial army and demoted to Yongzhou, where he looked up to heaven and wept.

sentences.zh: 賴先相公佐佑保援，方獲赦宥，若雷霆不收，承嗣豈有生理！

translations.literal: Only because the former lord aided and protected him did he obtain pardon; if thunder had not been withheld, how could Chengsi have lived!
translations.idiomatic: Only because the former lord aided and protected him did he obtain pardon. If thunder had not been withheld, how could Chengsi have lived!

sentences.zh: 今田悅兇狂，何如承嗣名望？

translations.literal: Now Tian Yue is fierce and reckless—how does he compare with Chengsi's renown?
translations.idiomatic: Now Tian Yue is fierce and reckless—how does he compare with Chengsi's renown?

sentences.zh: 茍欲坐邀富貴，不料破家覆族。

translations.literal: If you merely sit and seek wealth and honor, you do not consider the destruction of house and clan.
translations.idiomatic: If you merely sit and seek wealth and honor, you do not consider the destruction of house and clan.

sentences.zh: 而況今之將校，罕有義心，因利乘便，必相傾陷。

translations.literal: Moreover, today's commanders rarely have loyal hearts; seizing opportunity for profit, they are sure to overthrow and entrap one another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, today's commanders rarely have loyal hearts. Seizing opportunity for profit, they are sure to overthrow and entrap one another.

sentences.zh: 為大夫畫久長之計，莫若令惟誠知留後，大夫自速入朝。

translations.literal: To plan a long course for the lord, it would be best to have Weicheng made acting commissioner while the lord himself hurries to court.
translations.idiomatic: To plan a long course for the lord, it would be best to have Weicheng made acting commissioner while the lord himself hurries to court.

sentences.zh: 國家念先相公之功，見大夫順命，何求而不得？

translations.literal: The state, mindful of the former lord's merit and seeing the lord obey orders, what could you not obtain?
translations.idiomatic: The state, mindful of the former lord's merit and seeing the lord obey orders—what could you not obtain?

sentences.zh: 今與群逆為自危之計，非保家之道也。」

translations.literal: Now you join rebels in a plan that endangers yourselves—this is not the way to preserve the house."
translations.idiomatic: Now you join rebels in a plan that endangers yourselves—this is not the way to preserve the house."

sentences.zh: 惟嶽亦素忌從政，皆不聽，竟與魏、齊謀叛。

translations.literal: Weiyue had long been jealous of Congzheng and would not listen; in the end he joined Wei and Qi in plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue had long been jealous of Congzheng and would not listen. In the end he joined Wei and Qi in plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 既而惟嶽大將張孝忠以郡歸國，朝廷以孝忠為成德軍節度使，仍詔硃滔與孝忠合勢討之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Weiyue's great general Zhang Xiaozhong submitted his commandery to the state; the court appointed Xiaozhong military commissioner of the Chengde Army and also ordered Zhu Tao and Xiaozhong to join forces to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Weiyue's great general Zhang Xiaozhong submitted his commandery to the state. The court appointed Xiaozhong military commissioner of the Chengde Army and also ordered Zhu Tao and Xiaozhong to join forces to attack him.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽以精甲屯束鹿以抗之，田悅遣大將孟佑率兵五千助惟嶽。

translations.literal: Weiyue stationed crack troops at Shulu to resist; Tian Yue sent the great general Meng You with five thousand men to aid Weiyue.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue stationed crack troops at Shulu to resist. Tian Yue sent the great general Meng You with five thousand men to aid Weiyue.

sentences.zh: 建中三年正月，硃滔、孝忠大破恆州軍於束鹿，惟嶽燒營而遁。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jianzhong, Zhu Tao and Xiaozhong heavily defeated the Hengzhou army at Shulu; Weiyue burned camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Jianzhong, Zhu Tao and Xiaozhong heavily defeated the Hengzhou army at Shulu. Weiyue burned camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽大將趙州刺史康日知以郡歸國，惟嶽乃令衙將衛常寧率士卒五千，兵馬使王武俊率騎軍八百同討日知。

translations.literal: Weiyue's great general, Zhao prefect Kang Rizhi, submitted his commandery to the state; Weiyue then ordered yamen general Wei Changning to lead five thousand soldiers and cavalry commander Wang Wujun to lead eight hundred horsemen to attack Rizhi together.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue's great general, Zhao prefect Kang Rizhi, submitted his commandery to the state. Weiyue then ordered yamen general Wei Changning to lead five thousand soldiers and cavalry commander Wang Wujun to lead eight hundred horsemen to attack Rizhi together.

sentences.zh: 武俊既出恆州，謂常寧曰：「武俊盡心於本使，大夫信讒，頗相猜忌，所謂朝不謀夕，豈圖生路！

translations.literal: After Wujun had left Hengzhou, he said to Changning: "Wujun has given his whole heart to his lord, yet the lord believes slander and is quite suspicious of me—the saying is that one does not plan past morning for evening; how can I hope for a way to live!
translations.idiomatic: After Wujun had left Hengzhou, he said to Changning, "Wujun has given his whole heart to his lord, yet the lord believes slander and is quite suspicious of me. As they say, one does not plan past morning for evening—how can I hope for a way to live!

sentences.zh: 且趙州用兵，捷與不捷，武俊不復入恆州矣！

translations.literal: Moreover, whether the campaign at Zhao succeeds or fails, Wujun will not enter Hengzhou again!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whether the campaign at Zhao succeeds or fails, Wujun will not enter Hengzhou again!

sentences.zh: 妻子任從屠滅，且以殘生往定州事張尚書去也，孰能持頸就戮！」

translations.literal: Let wife and children be slaughtered as they will; with what life remains I shall go to Dingzhou and serve Vice Director Zhang—that is all. Who can stretch his neck to the execution block!"
translations.idiomatic: Let wife and children be slaughtered as they will. With what life remains I shall go to Dingzhou and serve Vice Director Zhang—that is all. Who can stretch his neck to the execution block!"

sentences.zh: 常寧曰：「中丞以大夫不可事，且有詔書雲，斬大夫首者，以其官爵授。

translations.literal: Changning said: "The vice director holds that the lord cannot be served, and moreover there is an edict saying that whoever cuts off the lord's head will receive his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Changning said, "The vice director holds that the lord cannot be served, and moreover there is an edict saying that whoever cuts off the lord's head will receive his office and rank.

sentences.zh: 自大夫拒命已來，張尚書以易州歸國得節度使。

translations.literal: Since the lord defied orders, Vice Director Zhang submitted Yi Prefecture to the state and received the commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: Since the lord defied orders, Vice Director Zhang submitted Yi Prefecture to the state and received the commissionership.

sentences.zh: 今聞日知已得官爵。

translations.literal: Now I hear Rizhi has already received office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear Rizhi has already received office and rank.

sentences.zh: 觀大夫事勢，終為硃滔所滅。

translations.literal: Judging the lord's situation, in the end he will be destroyed by Zhu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the lord's situation, in the end he will be destroyed by Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 此際轉禍為福，莫若倒戈入使府，誅大夫以取富貴也。

translations.literal: At this juncture to turn calamity into fortune, nothing is better than turning swords inward into headquarters, killing the lord to win wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture to turn calamity into fortune, nothing is better than turning swords inward into headquarters, killing the lord to win wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 況大夫暗昧，左右誑惑，其實易圖。

translations.literal: Moreover the lord is dim and those around him deceive and mislead him—he is in truth easy to plot against.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the lord is dim and those around him deceive and mislead him—he is in truth easy to plot against.

sentences.zh: 事茍不捷，歸張尚書非晚。」

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, returning to Vice Director Zhang will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: If the affair does not succeed, returning to Vice Director Zhang will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 武俊然之。

translations.literal: Wujun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年閏正月，武俊與常寧自趙州回戈，達明至恆，武俊子士真應於內。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the third year, Wujun and Changning turned their swords back from Zhao Prefecture; at daybreak they reached Heng, and Wujun's son Shizhen responded from within.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of the third year, Wujun and Changning turned their swords back from Zhao Prefecture. At daybreak they reached Heng, and Wujun's son Shizhen responded from within.

sentences.zh: 武俊兵突入府署，遣虞任越劫擒惟嶽，縊死於戟門外。

translations.literal: Wujun's troops burst into headquarters; he sent Yu Renyue to seize Weiyue and strangled him outside the halberd gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun's troops burst into headquarters. He sent Yu Renyue to seize Weiyue and strangled him outside the halberd gate.

sentences.zh: 又誅惟嶽妻父鄭華及長慶、王他奴等二十余人，傳首京師。

translations.literal: He also executed Weiyue's father-in-law Zheng Hua and Changqing, Wang Tanu, and more than twenty others, and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also executed Weiyue's father-in-law Zheng Hua, Changqing, Wang Tanu, and more than twenty others, and sent the head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 惟誠，惟嶽異母兄，以父廕為殿中丞，累遷至檢校戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: Weicheng was Weiyue's elder half-brother; through his father's privilege he became Palace Gentleman, and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng was Weiyue's elder half-brother. Through his father's privilege he became Palace Gentleman and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 好儒書理道，寶臣愛之，委以軍事；

translations.literal: He loved Confucian books and the Way of governance; Baochen cherished him and entrusted military affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Confucian books and the Way of governance. Baochen cherished him and entrusted military affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 性謙厚，以惟嶽嫡嗣，讓而不受。

translations.literal: He was modest and generous; because Weiyue was the legitimate heir, he yielded and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest and generous. Because Weiyue was the legitimate heir, he yielded and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 同母妹嫁李正己子納。

translations.literal: A younger sister by the same mother married Li Zhengji's son Na.
translations.idiomatic: A younger sister by the same mother married Li Zhengji's son Na.

sentences.zh: 寶臣以其宗姓，請惟誠歸本姓，又令入仕於鄆州，為李納營田副使。

translations.literal: Baochen, because they shared a clan surname, asked Weicheng to resume his original surname and also had him enter service at Yan Prefecture as Li Na's deputy commissioner for military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen, because they shared a clan surname, asked Weicheng to resume his original surname and also had him enter service at Yan Prefecture as Li Na's deputy commissioner for military colonies.

sentences.zh: 歷兗、淄、濟、淮四州刺史，竟客死東平。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Yan, Zi, Ji, and Huai, and in the end died as a guest in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as prefect of Yan, Zi, Ji, and Huai, and in the end died as a guest in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 惟簡，寶臣第三子。

translations.literal: Weijian was Baochen's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian was Baochen's third son.

sentences.zh: 初，王武俊既誅惟嶽，又械惟簡送京師。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Wang Wujun had killed Weiyue, he also shackled Weijian and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wang Wujun had killed Weiyue, he also shackled Weijian and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 德宗拘於客省，防伺甚峻。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong detained him in the guest quarters with very strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong detained him in the guest quarters under very strict guard.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之亂，惟簡斬關而出，赴奉天。

translations.literal: In Zhu Ci's rebellion, Weijian cut through the gate and fled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhu Ci's rebellion, Weijian cut through the gate and fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，用為禁軍將。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong commended him and appointed him a general of the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong commended him and appointed him a general of the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 從渾瑊率師討賊，頻戰屢捷，加御史中丞。

translations.literal: Following Hun Jian in leading troops to attack the rebels, he fought repeatedly and won often, and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Following Hun Jian in leading troops to attack the rebels, he fought repeatedly and won often, and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 從幸山南，得「元從功臣」之號，封武安郡王。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to the south of the mountains, he received the title "Meritorious Minister of the Original Retinue" and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor to the south of the mountains, he received the title "Meritorious Minister of the Original Retinue" and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 後授左神威大將軍，轉天威統軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Great General of the Left Divine Martial Army and transferred to commander of the Heavenly Might Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Great General of the Left Divine Martial Army and transferred to commander of the Heavenly Might Army.

sentences.zh: 元和初，檢校戶部尚書、左金吾衛大將軍，充街使；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was Acting Minister of Revenue and Great General of the Left Golden Guard, and served as street commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was Acting Minister of Revenue and Great General of the Left Golden Guard, and served as street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄拜鳳翔隴右節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年正月卒，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子元本，生於貴族，輕薄無行。

translations.literal: His son Yuanben was born into the nobility and was frivolous and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanben was born into the nobility and was frivolous and without conduct.

sentences.zh: 初，張茂昭子克禮尚襄陽公主。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Maozhao's son Keli married Princess Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Maozhao's son Keli married Princess Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，主縱恣不法，常遊行市裏。

translations.literal: In the Changqing era the princess was wanton and lawless and often roamed the market streets.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changqing era the princess was wanton and lawless and often roamed the market streets.

sentences.zh: 有士族子薛樞、薛渾者，俱得幸於主。

translations.literal: There were gentlemen of good families, Xue Shu and Xue Hun, who both won the princess's favor.
translations.idiomatic: There were gentlemen of good families, Xue Shu and Xue Hun, who both won the princess's favor.

sentences.zh: 尤愛渾，每詣渾家，謁渾母行事姑之禮。

translations.literal: She especially loved Hun; whenever she went to Hun's house she paid respects to Hun's mother as to a mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: She especially loved Hun. Whenever she went to Hun's house she paid respects to Hun's mother as to a mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 有吏誰何者，即以厚賂啖之。

translations.literal: If any clerk questioned her, she bribed him heavily to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: If any clerk questioned her, she bribed him heavily to silence him.

sentences.zh: 渾與元本皆少年，遂相誘掖；

translations.literal: Hun and Yuanben were both young men and thus led one another astray.
translations.idiomatic: Hun and Yuanben were both young men and thus led one another astray.

sentences.zh: 元本亦得幸於主，出入主第。

translations.literal: Yuanben also won the princess's favor and came and went at the princess's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanben also won the princess's favor and came and went at the princess's residence.

sentences.zh: 張克禮不勝其忿，上表陳聞，乃召主幽於禁中。

translations.literal: Zhang Keli could not bear his rage and submitted a memorial reporting it; the princess was then summoned and confined within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Keli could not bear his rage and submitted a memorial reporting it. The princess was then summoned and confined within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 以元本功臣之後，得減死，杖六十，流象州。

translations.literal: Because Yuanben was the descendant of a meritorious minister, his death sentence was reduced; he was beaten sixty strokes and exiled to Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuanben was the descendant of a meritorious minister, his death sentence was reduced. He was beaten sixty strokes and exiled to Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 樞、渾以元本之故，亦從輕杖八十，長流崖州。

translations.literal: Shu and Hun, because of Yuanben, also received lighter punishment of eighty strokes and long exile to Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Hun, because of Yuanben, also received lighter punishment of eighty strokes and long exile to Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王武俊，契丹怒皆部落也。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun was of the Nujie tribe of the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun was of the Nujie tribe of the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 祖可訥幹，父路俱。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Keneghan; his father was Luju.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Keneghan; his father was Luju.

sentences.zh: 開元中，饒樂府都督李詩率其部落五千帳，與路俱南河襲冠帶，有詔褒美，從居薊。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Raole Protectorate commander Li Shi led his tribe of five thousand households south of the river to receive caps and belts; an edict praised this, and they settled at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era, Raole Protectorate commander Li Shi led his tribe of five thousand households south of the river to receive caps and belts. An edict praised this, and they settled at Ji.

sentences.zh: 武俊初號沒諾幹，年十五，能騎射。

translations.literal: Wujun was at first called Monuogan; at fifteen he could ride and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was at first called Monuogan. At fifteen he could ride and shoot.

sentences.zh: 上元中，為史思明恆州刺史李寶臣裨將。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was a deputy commander under Hengzhou prefect Li Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era he was a deputy commander under Hengzhou prefect Li Baochen.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，王師入井陘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying the imperial army entered Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying the imperial army entered Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 將平河朔，武俊謂寶臣曰：「以寡敵眾，以曲遇直，戰則離，守則潰，銳師遠鬥，庸可禦乎？」

translations.literal: About to pacify Hebei, Wujun said to Baochen: "With few against many, with the bent meeting the straight—fight and the army splits; hold and it collapses. Can crack troops fighting far away be resisted?"
translations.idiomatic: About to pacify Hebei, Wujun said to Baochen, "With few against many, with the bent meeting the straight—fight and the army splits; hold and it collapses. Can crack troops fighting far away be resisted?"

sentences.zh: 寶臣遂徹警備，以恆、定、深、趙、易，充本軍先鋒兵馬使。

translations.literal: Baochen then withdrew guards and with Heng, Ding, Shen, Zhao, and Yi served as vanguard cavalry commander of his own army.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen then withdrew guards and with Heng, Ding, Shen, Zhao, and Yi served as vanguard cavalry commander of his own army.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年，田承嗣因薛嵩死，兼有相、衛、磁、邢、洺五州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dali, when Tian Chengsi took advantage of Xue Song's death and also held Xiang, Wei, Ci, Xing, and Ming prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Dali, when Tian Chengsi took advantage of Xue Song's death and also held Xiang, Wei, Ci, Xing, and Ming prefectures.

sentences.zh: 承嗣遣將盧子期寇磁州，詔令寶臣與李正己、李勉、李承昭、田神玉、硃滔、李抱真各出兵討之。

translations.literal: Chengsi sent the general Lu Ziqi to raid Ci Prefecture; an edict ordered Baochen together with Li Zhengji, Li Mian, Li Chengzhao, Tian Shenyu, Zhu Tao, and Li Baozhen each to send troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi sent the general Lu Ziqi to raid Ci Prefecture. An edict ordered Baochen together with Li Zhengji, Li Mian, Li Chengzhao, Tian Shenyu, Zhu Tao, and Li Baozhen each to send troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 諸軍與子期戰於清水，大破之。

translations.literal: The allied armies fought Ziqi at Qingshui and heavily defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies fought Ziqi at Qingshui and heavily defeated him.

sentences.zh: 寶臣將有節生擒子期以獻。

translations.literal: Baochen's general You Jiesheng captured Ziqi alive and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen's general You Jiesheng captured Ziqi alive and presented him.

sentences.zh: 代宗嘉其功，使中貴人馬承倩賫詔宣勞。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong commended his merit and sent the inner attendant Ma Chengqian bearing an edict to proclaim his labors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong commended his merit and sent the inner attendant Ma Chengqian bearing an edict to proclaim his labors.

sentences.zh: 承倩將歸，止傳舍，寶臣親遺百縑。

translations.literal: When Chengqian was about to return, he stopped at the relay station; Baochen personally sent him a hundred rolls of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqian was about to return, he stopped at the relay station. Baochen personally sent him a hundred rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 承倩詬詈，擲出道中；

translations.literal: Chengqian reviled and cursed him and threw them out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian reviled and cursed him and threw them out on the road.

sentences.zh: 寶臣顧左右有愧色。

translations.literal: Baochen looked at those around him with shame on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen looked at those around him with shame on his face.

sentences.zh: 還休府中，諸將散歸，寶臣潛伺屏間，獨武俊佩刀立於門下。

translations.literal: Returning to rest in headquarters, the generals dispersed home; Baochen secretly watched from behind the screen—only Wujun stood at the gate with sword in belt.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to rest in headquarters, the generals dispersed home. Baochen secretly watched from behind the screen—only Wujun stood at the gate with sword in belt.

sentences.zh: 召入，解刀與語曰：「見向者頑豎乎？」

translations.literal: He summoned him in, ungirded his sword, and spoke with him: "Did you see that obstinate fellow just now?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned him in, ungirded his sword, and spoke with him, "Did you see that obstinate fellow just now?"

sentences.zh: 武俊曰：「今閣下有功尚爾，寇平後，天子以幅紙之詔召置京下，一匹夫耳，可乎？」

translations.literal: Wujun said: "Now though Your Excellency has merit, you are still treated thus; after the rebels are pacified, the Son of Heaven will summon you to the capital with an edict on a strip of paper—you will be a common man. Is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said, "Now though Your Excellency has merit, you are still treated thus. After the rebels are pacified, the Son of Heaven will summon you to the capital with an edict on a strip of paper—you will be a common man. Is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 寶臣曰：「為之若何？」

translations.literal: Baochen said: "What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: Baochen said, "What is to be done about it?"

sentences.zh: 武俊曰：「不如玩養承嗣，以為己資。」

translations.literal: Wujun said: "Better to play with and nurture Chengsi as your own resource."
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said, "Better to play with and nurture Chengsi as your own resource."

sentences.zh: 寶臣曰：「今與承嗣有釁矣，可推腹心哉？」

translations.literal: Baochen said: "Now there is already a breach with Chengsi—how can you open your heart to him?"
translations.idiomatic: Baochen said, "Now there is already a breach with Chengsi—how can you open your heart to him?"

sentences.zh: 武俊曰：「勢同患均，轉寇仇為父子，咳唾間。

translations.literal: Wujun said: "Your situations are the same and your perils equal—turning enemy into father and son takes no more than the time to spit.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said, "Your situations are the same and your perils equal—turning enemy into father and son takes no more than the time to spit.

sentences.zh: 若傳虛言，無益也。

translations.literal: If you only pass empty words, it is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If you only pass empty words, it is of no use.

sentences.zh: 今中貴人劉清譚在驛，斬首送承嗣，立質妻孥矣！」

translations.literal: Now the inner attendant Liu Qingtan is at the relay station—cut off his head and send it to Chengsi, and establish his wife and children as hostages!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the inner attendant Liu Qingtan is at the relay station—cut off his head and send it to Chengsi, and establish his wife and children as hostages!"

sentences.zh: 寶臣曰：「恐不能如此。」

translations.literal: Baochen said: "I fear it cannot be done thus."
translations.idiomatic: Baochen said, "I fear it cannot be done thus."

sentences.zh: 武俊曰：「硃滔為國屯兵滄州，請擒送承嗣以取信。」

translations.literal: Wujun said: "Zhu Tao is garrisoning troops at Cangzhou for the state—ask to seize and send him to Chengsi to win trust."
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said, "Zhu Tao is garrisoning troops at Cangzhou for the state—ask to seize and send him to Chengsi to win trust."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: He agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 立選士二千，皆乘駿馬，通夜馳三百里，晨至滔營，掩其不備。

translations.literal: He selected two thousand picked men, all mounted on swift horses; they galloped three hundred li through the night and at dawn reached Tao's camp and struck while he was unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: He selected two thousand picked men, all mounted on swift horses. They galloped three hundred li through the night and at dawn reached Tao's camp and struck while he was unprepared.

sentences.zh: 滔軍出戰，大敗，擒類滔者，滔故得脫。

translations.literal: Tao's army came out to fight and was heavily defeated; they captured one resembling Tao, and Tao himself escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's army came out to fight and was heavily defeated. They captured one resembling Tao, and Tao himself escaped.

sentences.zh: 自此寶臣與田承嗣、李正己更相為援，皆武俊萌之。

translations.literal: From this Baochen with Tian Chengsi and Li Zhengji alternately supported one another—all this Wujun had set in motion.
translations.idiomatic: From this Baochen with Tian Chengsi and Li Zhengji alternately supported one another—all this Wujun had set in motion.

sentences.zh: 寶臣死，其子惟嶽謀襲父位。

translations.literal: When Baochen died, his son Weiyue plotted to seize his father's position.
translations.idiomatic: When Baochen died, his son Weiyue plotted to seize his father's position.

sentences.zh: 寶臣舊將易州刺史張孝忠以州順命，遂以孝忠代寶臣。

translations.literal: Baochen's old general, Yi Prefecture prefect Zhang Xiaozhong, submitted his prefecture in obedience to orders; Xiaozhong was then made to replace Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen's old general, Yi Prefecture prefect Zhang Xiaozhong, submitted his prefecture in obedience to orders. Xiaozhong was then made to replace Baochen.

sentences.zh: 俾惟嶽護喪歸京，惟嶽不受命。

translations.literal: Weiyue was ordered to escort the funeral to the capital; Weiyue would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue was ordered to escort the funeral to the capital; Weiyue would not obey.

sentences.zh: 建中三年正月，詔硃滔、張孝忠合軍討之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jianzhong, an edict ordered Zhu Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong to join armies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Jianzhong, an edict ordered Zhu Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong to join armies to attack him.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽與武俊復統萬余眾戰於束鹿。

translations.literal: Weiyue and Wujun again commanded more than ten thousand men and fought at Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue and Wujun again commanded more than ten thousand men and fought at Shulu.

sentences.zh: 武俊率三千騎先進，為滔所敗，惟嶽遁走。

translations.literal: Wujun led three thousand horsemen in the van and was defeated by Tao; Weiyue fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun led three thousand horsemen in the van and was defeated by Tao. Weiyue fled.

sentences.zh: 趙州刺史康日知遂以州順命，惟嶽令武俊統兵擊之。

translations.literal: Zhao prefect Kang Rizhi then submitted his prefecture in obedience to orders; Weiyue ordered Wujun to command troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao prefect Kang Rizhi then submitted his prefecture in obedience to orders. Weiyue ordered Wujun to command troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 日知遣人謂武俊曰：「惟嶽孱微而無謀，何足同反！

translations.literal: Rizhi sent a man to say to Wujun: "Weiyue is feeble and without strategy—why join him in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi sent a man to say to Wujun, "Weiyue is feeble and without strategy—why join him in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 我城堅眾一，未可以歲月下。

translations.literal: My walls are strong and my people united; you cannot take the city in a year.
translations.idiomatic: My walls are strong and my people united—you cannot take the city in a year.

sentences.zh: 且惟嶽恃田悅為援，前歲悅之丁男甲卒塗地於邢州城下，猶不能陷，況此城乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover Weiyue relies on Tian Yue as support; last year Yue's young men and armored soldiers lay dead in heaps below Xingzhou's walls and still could not breach it—how much less this city!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Weiyue relies on Tian Yue as support. Last year Yue's young men and armored soldiers lay dead in heaps below Xingzhou's walls and still could not breach it—how much less this city!"

sentences.zh: 復給偽手詔招武俊，信之；

translations.literal: He also sent a forged handwritten edict to recruit Wujun; Wujun believed it.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a forged handwritten edict to recruit Wujun; Wujun believed it.

sentences.zh: 遂倒兵入恆州，率數百騎入衙門。

translations.literal: He then turned his army into Hengzhou and led several hundred horsemen into the yamen gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned his army into Hengzhou and led several hundred horsemen into the yamen gate.

sentences.zh: 使謂惟嶽曰：「大夫舉兵與魏、齊同惡，今田尚書已喪敗，李尚書為趙州所間，軍士自束鹿之役，傷痛軫心。

translations.literal: He sent someone to say to Weiyue: "The lord raised troops in evil union with Wei and Qi; now Vice Minister Tian has already been defeated, Vice Minister Li has been estranged by Zhao Prefecture, and since the battle at Shulu the soldiers' wounds and grief pierce the heart.
translations.idiomatic: He sent someone to say to Weiyue, "The lord raised troops in evil union with Wei and Qi. Now Vice Minister Tian has already been defeated, Vice Minister Li has been estranged by Zhao Prefecture, and since the battle at Shulu the soldiers' wounds and grief pierce the heart.

sentences.zh: 硃僕射強兵宿境內，張尚書已授定州，三軍俱懼殞首喪家。

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhu has strong troops encamped within the borders; Vice Director Zhang has already been given Ding Prefecture; the three armies all fear losing their heads and destroying their houses.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhu has strong troops encamped within the borders. Vice Director Zhang has already been given Ding Prefecture. The three armies all fear losing their heads and destroying their houses.

sentences.zh: 聞有詔征大夫，宜亟赴命，不爾，禍在漏刻。」

translations.literal: Word has come of an edict summoning the lord—you should hurry to obey orders; otherwise disaster falls within the hour."
translations.idiomatic: Word has come of an edict summoning the lord—you should hurry to obey orders. Otherwise disaster falls within the hour."

sentences.zh: 惟嶽怖，遽睢盱。

translations.literal: Weiyue was terrified and stared about in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue was terrified and stared about in panic.

sentences.zh: 武俊子士真斬惟嶽，持首而出。

translations.literal: Wujun's son Shizhen cut off Weiyue's head and came out holding it.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun's son Shizhen cut off Weiyue's head and came out holding it.

sentences.zh: 武俊殺不同己者十數人，遂定。

translations.literal: Wujun killed more than ten who did not agree with him and then stabilized the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun killed more than ten who did not agree with him and then stabilized the situation.

sentences.zh: 傳首上聞，授武俊檢校秘書少監、兼御史大夫、恆州刺史、恆冀都團練觀察使，實封五百戶，以康日知為深趙團練觀察使。

translations.literal: He sent the head to report to the court; Wujun was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, prefect of Hengzhou, and Commissioner for Heng and Ji, with a substantive fief of five hundred households; Kang Rizhi was made Commissioner for Shen and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the head to report to the court. Wujun was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, prefect of Hengzhou, and Commissioner for Heng and Ji, with a substantive fief of five hundred households. Kang Rizhi was made Commissioner for Shen and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 時惟嶽偽定州刺史楊政義以州順命，深州刺史楊榮國降硃滔，分兵鎮之。

translations.literal: At that time Weiyue's false Ding Prefecture prefect Yang Zhengyi submitted his prefecture in obedience to orders; Shen Prefecture prefect Yang Rongguo surrendered to Zhu Tao, and troops were divided to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Weiyue's false Ding Prefecture prefect Yang Zhengyi submitted his prefecture in obedience to orders. Shen Prefecture prefect Yang Rongguo surrendered to Zhu Tao, and troops were divided to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷既以定州屬張孝忠．深州屬康日知。

translations.literal: The court had already assigned Ding Prefecture to Zhang Xiaozhong and Shen Prefecture to Kang Rizhi.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already assigned Ding Prefecture to Zhang Xiaozhong and Shen Prefecture to Kang Rizhi.

sentences.zh: 武俊怒失趙、定二州，且名位不滿其誌。

translations.literal: Wujun was angry at losing Zhao and Ding prefectures and that his name and rank did not satisfy his ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was angry at losing Zhao and Ding prefectures and that his name and rank did not satisfy his ambition.

sentences.zh: 硃滔怒失深州，因誘武俊謀反，斥言朝廷，遂連率勁兵救田悅。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao was angry at losing Shen Prefecture; he therefore enticed Wujun to plot rebellion, spoke harshly of the court, and then led crack troops in succession to rescue Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao was angry at losing Shen Prefecture. He therefore enticed Wujun to plot rebellion, spoke harshly of the court, and then led crack troops in succession to rescue Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 時馬燧、李抱真、李芃、李晟方討田悅，敗悅於洹水。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Sui, Li Baozhen, Li Qi, and Li Sheng were attacking Tian Yue and defeated him at Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Sui, Li Baozhen, Li Qi, and Li Sheng were attacking Tian Yue and defeated him at Huanshui.

sentences.zh: 後連歲暴兵，然悅勢已蹙。

translations.literal: Afterward they waged war for successive years, yet Yue's position was already pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they waged war for successive years, yet Yue's position was already pressed.

sentences.zh: 至是武俊、硃滔復振起之。

translations.literal: Now Wujun and Zhu Tao revived him again.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wujun and Zhu Tao revived him again.

sentences.zh: 悅勢益張。

translations.literal: Yue's power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's power grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 十一月，武俊使大將張鐘葵寇趙州，康日知擊敗之，斬首上獻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Wujun sent the great general Zhang Zhongkui to raid Zhao Prefecture; Kang Rizhi defeated him and sent the severed head to present.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wujun sent the great general Zhang Zhongkui to raid Zhao Prefecture. Kang Rizhi defeated him and sent the severed head to present.

sentences.zh: 是日，武俊僭建國，稱趙王，又恆州為真定府，偽命官秩。

translations.literal: That day Wujun presumptuously established a state, styled himself King of Zhao, also made Hengzhou the capital Zhending, and falsely appointed offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: That day Wujun presumptuously established a state, styled himself King of Zhao, made Hengzhou the capital Zhending, and falsely appointed offices and ranks.

sentences.zh: 硃滔、田悅、李納一同僭號，分據所部，各遣使勸誘蔡州李希烈同僭位號。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao, Tian Yue, and Li Na likewise presumptuously assumed titles, each holding his own territory, and each sent envoys to persuade Li Xilie at Caizhou to join in assuming titles.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao, Tian Yue, and Li Na likewise presumptuously assumed titles, each holding his own territory, and each sent envoys to persuade Li Xilie at Caizhou to join in assuming titles.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，希烈既為周曾謀潰其腹心，或傳希烈已死，馬燧等四節度軍中聞之，歡聲震外。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, after Xilie had been undermined by Zhou Zeng's plot against his inner circle, or when word spread that Xilie was dead, the four commissioners' armies heard it and cheers shook the camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, after Xilie had been undermined by Zhou Zeng's plot against his inner circle, or when word spread that Xilie was dead, the four commissioners' armies heard it and cheers shook the camp.

sentences.zh: 六月，李抱真使辯客賈林詐降武俊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Li Baozhen sent the eloquent guest Jia Lin to feign surrender to Wujun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Baozhen sent the eloquent guest Jia Lin to feign surrender to Wujun.

sentences.zh: 林至武俊壁曰：「是來傳詔，非降也。」

translations.literal: Lin came to Wujun's rampart and said: "I have come to transmit an edict—not to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Lin came to Wujun's rampart and said, "I have come to transmit an edict—not to surrender."

sentences.zh: 武俊色動，征其說。

translations.literal: Wujun's expression changed and he pressed for his explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun's expression changed and he pressed for his explanation.

sentences.zh: 林曰：「天子知大夫宿誠，及登壇建國之日，撫膺顧左右曰：『我本忠義，天子不省。』

translations.literal: Lin said: "The Son of Heaven knows the lord's long-standing loyalty; on the day you mounted the altar and established the state, he beat his breast and looked at those around him and said, 'I was always loyal—the Son of Heaven did not understand.'
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "The Son of Heaven knows the lord's long-standing loyalty. On the day you mounted the altar and established the state, he beat his breast and looked at those around him and said, 'I was always loyal—the Son of Heaven did not understand.'

sentences.zh: 是後諸軍曾同表論列大夫。

translations.literal: Afterward the armies jointly submitted memorials on the lord's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the armies jointly submitted memorials on the lord's behalf.

sentences.zh: 天子覽表動容，語使者曰：『朕前事誤，追無及已。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven read the memorials with moved expression and said to the envoy: 'I was wrong before—there is no catching up now.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven read the memorials with moved expression and said to the envoy, 'I was wrong before—there is no catching up now.

sentences.zh: 朋友間失意尚可謝，朕四海主，毫芒安可復念哉！』」

translations.literal: Between friends, if one is disappointed, one can still apologize; I am lord of the four seas—how can I dwell on a hair's breadth!'"
translations.idiomatic: Between friends, if one is disappointed, one can still apologize. I am lord of the four seas—how can I dwell on a hair's breadth!'"

sentences.zh: 武俊曰：「仆虜將，尚知存撫百姓，天子固不專務殺人以安天下。

translations.literal: Wujun said: "I, a captive general, still know to cherish and comfort the people; the Son of Heaven surely does not devote himself solely to killing men to pacify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said, "I, a captive general, still know to cherish and comfort the people. The Son of Heaven surely does not devote himself solely to killing men to pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 今山東大兵者五，比戰勝，骨盡暴野，雖勝與誰守？

translations.literal: Now there are five great armies east of the mountains; even when they win, the bones lie exposed across the wild—though you win, with whom will you hold the land?
translations.idiomatic: Now there are five great armies east of the mountains. Even when they win, the bones lie exposed across the wild—though you win, with whom will you hold the land?

sentences.zh: 今不憚歸國，以與諸侯盟約，虜性直，不欲曲在己。

translations.literal: Now I do not fear returning to the state and making covenant with the feudal lords; my barbarian nature is straight and I do not wish the fault to lie with me.
translations.idiomatic: Now I do not fear returning to the state and making covenant with the feudal lords. My barbarian nature is straight and I do not wish the fault to lie with me.

sentences.zh: 朝廷能降恩滌蕩之，仆首倡歸國，不從者，於以奉辭，則上不負天子，下不負朋友。

translations.literal: If the court can lower grace and wash away offenses, I will be first to lead the return to the state; those who do not follow, I will take arms against them—then above I will not fail the Son of Heaven, below I will not fail my friends.
translations.idiomatic: If the court can lower grace and wash away offenses, I will be first to lead the return to the state. Those who do not follow, I will take arms against them—then above I will not fail the Son of Heaven, below I will not fail my friends.

sentences.zh: 此謀既行，河朔不五旬可定。」

translations.literal: Once this plan is carried out, Hebei can be settled within fifty days."
translations.idiomatic: Once this plan is carried out, Hebei can be settled within fifty days."

sentences.zh: 十月，涇原兵犯闕，上幸奉天。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Jingyuan army violated the capital; the emperor fled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Jingyuan army violated the capital. The emperor fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 京師問至，諸將退軍。

translations.literal: When word from the capital arrived, the generals withdrew their armies.
translations.idiomatic: When word from the capital arrived, the generals withdrew their armies.

sentences.zh: 李抱真將還潞澤，田悅說武俊與硃滔襲擊之。

translations.literal: As Li Baozhen was about to return to Lu and Ze, Tian Yue persuaded Wujun and Zhu Tao to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Baozhen was about to return to Lu and Ze, Tian Yue persuaded Wujun and Zhu Tao to strike him.

sentences.zh: 賈林復說武俊曰：「今退軍前輜重，後銳師，人心固一，不可圖也。

translations.literal: Jia Lin again persuaded Wujun: "Now the army withdraws with baggage in front and crack troops behind; hearts are firmly united—it cannot be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lin again persuaded Wujun, "Now the army withdraws with baggage in front and crack troops behind. Hearts are firmly united—it cannot be plotted against.

sentences.zh: 且勝而得地，則利歸魏博；

translations.literal: Moreover if you win and gain land, the profit goes to Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover if you win and gain land, the profit goes to Weibo.

sentences.zh: 喪師，即成德大傷。

translations.literal: If you lose the army, it is a great wound to Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: If you lose the army, it is a great wound to Chengde.

sentences.zh: 大夫本部易、定、滄、趙四州，何不先復故地？」

translations.literal: The lord's own territory is the four prefectures Yi, Ding, Cang, and Zhao—why not first recover the old lands?"
translations.idiomatic: The lord's own territory is the four prefectures Yi, Ding, Cang, and Zhao—why not first recover the old lands?"

sentences.zh: 武俊遂北馬首，背田悅約。

translations.literal: Wujun then turned his horse north and broke his covenant with Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun then turned his horse north and broke his covenant with Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 賈林復說武俊曰：「大夫冀邦豪族，不合謀據中華。

translations.literal: Jia Lin again persuaded Wujun: "The lord is a great clan of Ji—he should not plot to hold the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lin again persuaded Wujun, "The lord is a great clan of Ji—he should not plot to hold the central lands.

sentences.zh: 且滔心幽險，王室強即藉大夫援之，卑即思有並吞。

translations.literal: Moreover Tao's heart is dark and treacherous; when the royal house is strong he borrows the lord's aid, when it is weak he thinks of swallowing you.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Tao's heart is dark and treacherous. When the royal house is strong he borrows the lord's aid; when it is weak he thinks of swallowing you.

sentences.zh: 且河朔無冀國，唯趙、魏、燕耳！

translations.literal: Moreover in Hebei there is no Ji state—only Zhao, Wei, and Yan!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in Hebei there is no Ji state—only Zhao, Wei, and Yan!

sentences.zh: 今硃滔稱冀，則窺大夫冀州，其兆已形矣。

translations.literal: Now Zhu Tao styles himself Ji—the sign that he covets the lord's Ji Prefecture has already taken shape.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhu Tao styles himself Ji—the sign that he covets the lord's Ji Prefecture has already taken shape.

sentences.zh: 若滔力制山東，大夫須整臣禮；

translations.literal: If Tao by force controls the east of the mountains, the lord must arrange himself in minister's ritual.
translations.idiomatic: If Tao by force controls the east of the mountains, the lord must arrange himself in minister's ritual.

sentences.zh: 不從，即為所攻奪，此時臣滔乎？」

translations.literal: If you do not obey, he will attack and seize you—at that time will you be Tao's minister?"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not obey, he will attack and seize you—at that time will you be Tao's minister?"

sentences.zh: 武俊投袂作色曰：「二百年宗社，我尚不能臣，誰能臣田舍漢！」

translations.literal: Wujun flung his sleeve and changed color: "A two-hundred-year dynasty—I still cannot serve it as minister; who could serve a rustic Han!"
translations.idiomatic: Wujun flung his sleeve and changed color. "A two-hundred-year dynasty—I still cannot serve it as minister. Who could serve a rustic Han!"

sentences.zh: 由此計定，遂南修好抱真，西連盟馬燧。

translations.literal: From this the plan was settled; he then made peace with Baozhen to the south and allied with Ma Sui to the west.
translations.idiomatic: From this the plan was settled. He then made peace with Baozhen to the south and allied with Ma Sui to the west.

sentences.zh: 會興元元年德宗罪己，大赦反側。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan Emperor Dezong blamed himself and issued a great amnesty for rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan Emperor Dezong blamed himself and issued a great amnesty for rebels.

sentences.zh: 二月，武俊集三軍，削偽國號。

translations.literal: In the second month Wujun assembled the three armies and cast off the false state title.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wujun assembled the three armies and cast off the false state title.

sentences.zh: 詔國子祭酒兼御史大夫董晉、中使王進傑，自行在至恆州宣命，授武俊檢校兵部尚書、成德軍節度使。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Imperial Diagnostician and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief Dong Jin and the inner attendant Wang Jinjie to go from the imperial camp to Hengzhou to proclaim the appointment of Wujun as Acting Minister of War and military commissioner of the Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Imperial Diagnostician and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief Dong Jin and the inner attendant Wang Jinjie to go from the imperial camp to Hengzhou to proclaim the appointment of Wujun as Acting Minister of War and military commissioner of the Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 三月，加司空、同中書門下平章事，兼幽州、盧龍兩道節度使、瑯邪郡王。

translations.literal: In the third month he was further made Minister of Works, Co-commissioner of the Department of State Affairs and the Chancellery, and military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was further made Minister of Works, Co-commissioner of the Department of State Affairs and the Chancellery, and military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 時硃泚偽冊滔為皇太弟，滔率幽、檀勁卒，誘回紇二千騎，已圍貝州數十日，將絕白馬津，南盜洛都，與泚合勢。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Ci falsely enfeoffed Tao as Imperial Younger Brother; Tao led crack troops of You and Tan and enticed two thousand Uyghur horsemen, had already besieged Beizhou for several tens of days, and was about to cut the Baima ford and raid south to Luoyang to join forces with Ci.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Ci falsely enfeoffed Tao as Imperial Younger Brother. Tao led crack troops of You and Tan and enticed two thousand Uyghur horsemen, had already besieged Beizhou for several tens of days, and was about to cut the Baima ford and raid south to Luoyang to join forces with Ci.

sentences.zh: 時李懷光反，據河中；
